_comment: Storage: the immutable, volatile, UTxO and ledger snapshot stores, the Haskell database and snapshot import, SCLS and Mithril (module storage). Its reference is ouroboros-consensus's storage layer and cardano-ledger's state encoders. Mapping it adds entries only: its code is under the format freeze (FMT-1). docs/design/correspondence-map.md says what an entry holds; scripts/check_correspondence.py checks it.

given storage.haskell.state.ConsensusCod.note: version 1 and nine fields, the ninth the announcement as encodeStrictMaybe encodeAnnouncedBy ([] or [[issuer, hash, size]]), the bytes the reference writes; the types differ: Praos2.State holds Praos's eight fields as a PraosState with the announcement beside them where the reference's record is flat, and the announced size is a Long checked to a Word32 on writing where the reference holds a Word32. The 11.1 layout has no Praos2 and does not write one. LeiosLayoutSuite reads the Praos2 state of a captured Leios devnet state (no announcement), checks each of its nine fields against the values read off the file's raw bytes, and writes it back byte for byte; it reads and writes the public testnet's state at slot 2,168,639 whole, whose Praos2 state holds an announcement

def storage.haskell.state.Params.codecIn.note: the 11.1 layout's Dijkstra parameters (35 items, cardano-ledger f649f975 eras/dijkstra/impl/src/Cardano/Ledger/Dijkstra/PParams.hs:423-459) are refused (DijkstraNotYet.LedgerState), which the reference decodes; 11.x never enters Dijkstra, its major-version cap being 11. The Leios build's 54 are read and written byte for byte, every era's parameters held in one flat ProtocolParams, each field at the range of the reference's field type

def storage.haskell.state.Wire.unitInter.note: a Rational in the interval's bounds, not a newtype over BoundedRatio; the numbers are read as Word64 from version 12 and as Integer before it

def storage.haskell.state.Wire.nonNegati.note: a Rational in the interval's bounds, not a newtype over BoundedRatio; the numbers are read as Word64 from version 12 and as Integer before it

def storage.haskell.state.Wire.positiveI.note: a Rational in the interval's bounds, not a newtype over BoundedRatio; the numbers are read as Word64 from version 12 and as Integer before it

class storage.FileImmutableStore.IndexCa.note: the reference's past chunks (an IntPSQ by time of last use) and their number, bounded at 250 chunks; here a map by chunk with an index ordered by (time of last use, order of use), and the number of entries held, bounded at 270,000 entries; the chunk appended to is held apart, in Current, as currentChunkInfo is. ImmutableServingSuite checks the approved policy; no suite compares it with the reference, whose bound it departs from by decision

def storage.FileImmutableStore.IndexCach.note: the reference adds a chunk, then drops the least recently used one if more than 250 are held (composed at getChunkInfo and openPrimaryIndex); here it adds the chunk, then drops the least recently used until the entries held are within the bound, and does not hold an index larger than the bound. ImmutableServingSuite checks the approved policy; no suite compares it with the reference, whose bound it departs from by decision

garbageCollect's decision: every chunk last used at or before now less the expiry is dropped; here by walking the cache's index ordered by last use, where the reference takes a view of its IntPSQ, and with the age taken as now less the use; the trace event (TracePastChunksExpired) is not emitted, as the store emits none of the cache's TraceCacheEvent. ImmutableServingSuite checks the expiry over time under TestControl; no suite compares it with the reference

val storage.FileImmutableStore.IndexCach.note: the past chunks' part of emptyCached; the chunk appended to is held apart, in Current

def storage.ImmutableStore#refOf.note: getBlockComponent for the components a point's index entry answers (GetSlot, GetHash, GetIsEBB): getSlotInfo finds the point in the primary and secondary indexes and extractBlockComponent answers them from the entry, the block not read. Here one method gives the entry's slot, hash, boundary flag and block number (which the reference's secondary index does not hold), found in the chunk's entries as the store holds them, and the chunk file is not opened (the reference opens it, Impl.hs 466-469). HaskellImportSuite compares what it finds, for every block and for another hash at each slot, with the reference's own primary and secondary indexes: the Preview ImmutableDB cardano-node 11.1.3 wrote, and a Byron-to-Conway database with boundary blocks written by the reference's encoding rules; the other suites check that no block is read

def storage.haskell.state.Envelope.teles.note: one Past per finished era and then the Current, 1 + era index items, the era of the current state its length, as the reference's; the telescope is built with Telescope.make, so the eras abut. In the Leios build's layout every era is read and written, Dijkstra among them (LeiosLayoutSuite: the captured Dijkstra states byte for byte); in the 11.1 layout a telescope in Dijkstra is refused both ways (DijkstraNotYet.LedgerState), which the reference decodes; 11.x never enters Dijkstra, its major-version cap being 11

given storage.haskell.state.LedgerFileCo.note: [era index, the era's tip], a Shelley-based tip [slot, hash, block number] and Byron's with the boundary flag after them, as the reference's NS of the eras' AnnTip codecs; the model holds one AnnTip with a TipInfo per era kind where the reference's is per era. In the Leios build's layout a Dijkstra tip (era 7) is read and written (LeiosLayoutSuite, the captured Dijkstra states); in the 11.1 layout it is refused both ways (DijkstraNotYet.LedgerState), which the reference decodes

val storage.haskell.state.ConsensusCodec.note: the ledger state of the era at a telescope's index: a Shelley-based era's [2, [tip, NewEpochState, transition, fourth field]] read into the mirror, Byron's ChainValidationState kept as the original item (not modelled, so written as read). Dijkstra's is read and written in the Leios build's layout, at version 12 (LeiosLayoutSuite, the captured Dijkstra states byte for byte), and refused both ways in the 11.1 layout (DijkstraNotYet.LedgerState), which the reference decodes

given storage.haskell.state.CertStateCod.note: nine items written by the node's parameters' codec (poolParams), so the bytes of parameters without a key are those written before (FuturePoolParamsCodecSuite, both layouts). Read by that codec, then as the reference reads the two fields it keeps unread: the metadata as DecCBOR PoolMetadata at the state's version (PoolMetadata.read: a [url, hash] record, the url bounded by the version and its text chunked only in the Leios layout from version 12, the hash chunked from 12 in both) and the account's network 0 or 1 (decodeAccountAddressT, Address.hs:930-948 at f649f975), each refused with a typed error; the owner decided on 2026-11-19 (asked 19:18:13Z, decided 20:18:03Z, #85 item 38) that the state read matches the reference here. In the Leios layout from version 12 the voting key is read where the third of ten items is a list (decodeStakePoolParamsFlat) and written as ten items with the key third (withStakePoolParamsFlatEncoding, through ConwayCodecs.poolFieldsWith); below version 12 it is not written, as the reference drops it. Keyed parameters have their relays read as the reference reads them (PoolRelays.fromState); keyless ones keep the earlier reader, which takes any array and keeps its bytes. Reading and writing the key was approved under the format freeze on 2026-11-20 (#54), V10 changed in place

def storage.haskell.state.ConwayCodecs.p.note: the flat fields with a third written after the VRF key hash, the voting key's place; the caller writes the list length and the key, where the reference computes both from the encoding version

def storage.haskell.state.NodeTypeCodecs.note: the ten items with the third read by the slot's codec: none for the node's parameters (refused as DijkstraNotYet.PoolParamsBlsKey where it is a key), the key for the state's parameters; the reference peeks at the third item's type instead

class storage.ReceivedBlocks.Linked.note: the block's reference (hash, slot, number, boundary) and its predecessor, the fields of BlockInfo the iterator's path walk reads; the header's offset and size, which the reference keeps to read a header alone, are not kept. Evidence: the wire cases of ChainServerSuite assert each outcome of the reference's ChainDB iterator and BlockFetch server, as their source at the pins gives it, over a connection Scarab serves; no running reference node is asked

def storage.VolatileStore.openIndexWith.note: as parseBlockFile and extractBlockInfo, each block is read in turn and its location kept with what is read from its body (here the predecessor). It differs in the recovery it shares with openIndex: the first damaged file is cut and every file after it removed, where the reference's open (mkOpenStateHelper) truncates each damaged file and keeps the others, and truncates a later file at a block already indexed: a Gap (#1247), to be aligned for the received log; the selected-chain journal keeps its in-order recovery

glue.reason: Groups Dijkstra wire codecs and validates constructed values by decoding their serialization with the production ledger decoder and comparing values. The encoded forms are mapped separately; these codecs are not persisted-state formats.
the decimal numbers in Scarab's own storage file names, written in ASCII digits under every locale; the reference writes the numbers of its own file names with show, which writes ASCII digits

the numbers of Scarab's own storage file names read back from ASCII digits only, and a name in a locale's digits refused as a typed error; the reference reads the numbers of its own file names with readMaybe, which takes ASCII digits only, and passes over a name it cannot read

the frozen kinds of a stored script in the sidecar schemas of the snapshot versions before V10, and the script's codec over a kind's codec: Scarab's own persisted format, which keeps the bytes and fingerprints of its previous files; the reference keeps no such files and has no counterpart (#85, #54)

the frozen chain-dependent states in the sidecar schemas of the snapshot versions before V10, and the native codecs of Praos2's state: Scarab's own persisted format, which keeps the bytes and fingerprints of its previous files; the reference keeps no such files and has no counterpart (#826)
fills the parameters an era does not have from genesis, so that the node's one flat ProtocolParams is complete after an import; the reference holds each era's own record and has no such step (#826)

the ten items of a StakePoolParams of the Leios layout from version 12 whose third holds no BLS key, and their conversion to the held nine; Scarab's PoolParams has no key, so the reader that uses them (NodeTypeCodecs.poolParams, which cites decodeStakePoolParamsFlat, cardano-ledger 9df9f98c State/StakePool.hs:744-771) reads ten items through this record
plumbing: the immutable store's reads of its own chunk and index files (Scarab's own format) as an algebra with one interpreter over fs2's Files, so that a suite can count what serving a block reads
plumbing: the companion object that holds the empty index cache of the immutable store

plumbing: a fiber for the life of a resource that ends with its failure as a value (FIB-2), raised again where it is landed and at release; it runs the index cache's expiry, which the reference starts with forkLinkedThread (Index/Cache.hs 428-432, ouroboros-consensus 82ecba32), whose link throws a failure to the owner at once, where here the owner meets it at release; the expiry has no failure of its own

the admission of a ledger state that enters the node from a snapshot or an import, refusing one that no chain of the configured reference build reaches and that its rules would carry to another state than the reference's, and the snapshot format that applies it as a state comes in; the reference has no such check, no chain it runs reaching such a state (it decodes PState as it is, State/CertState.hs 257-265, cardano-ledger f649f975); refused rather than repaired by the owner's decision (asked 2026-11-18T08:22:34Z and decided 2026-11-18T14:21:46Z), docs/running/snapshots.md#unreachable-ledger-state

the store's own RocksDB layout of the Leios store format approved for #830 and changed for its exact round trip (a meta column family with the format record, and per partition the column families of the reference's ebs, ebBodies and ebClosures tables, the closure's written transactions, and the volatile closures' completion; opening, release and the in-memory rows of the volatile partition); the reference keeps the same records in its two SQLite files

what an import from or an export to the reference's SQLite files exchanges with the store, one endorser block at a time, the rows, body and closure of each partition as its tables hold them, through an open that resumes nothing, so a pending copy or sweep is exchanged as it is; the reference has no import or export of its LeiosDB
closed typed errors and their messages, where the reference throws a LeiosDbException with a message (ERR-1)
accessors of a body and of a status byte, which the reference reads inline from the vector of its LeiosEb and from the status column

how the store's RocksDB keeps the reference's guarantees: a read through a snapshot (the reference reads inside one SQLite transaction, dbWithTransaction), the volatile partition's rows held in memory with the volatile and copied ones a mark visits and the hashes with a marked row (its idx_ebs_sweepable and idx_ebs_markedForGc indexes), the size of a collection's batch, and the staging directory a new store is made in and published from by an atomic rename
a body's equality, hash and text, the ones its case class had, which it no longer is so that no product mirror can make one unchecked

the export's reading of the store from one snapshot, and a first open: under an exclusive operating-system lock on a file beside the store, a new store made in a marked staging directory and published by an atomic rename, and the parent directory synced before a store is taken; the reference reads inside one SQLite transaction, creates its files in place (initialiseLeiosDbFiles) with SQLite's own locking, and has no export

the permits that keep a process's first opens of one Leios store apart, one per lock file, before its operating-system lock is taken: that lock belongs to the process, so it cannot exclude another open of the same process; an instance the caller makes once for the process (EFF-4); the reference's SQLite files have SQLite's own locking, and it has no such permits
the import and export of the reference's SQLite files, which the reference does not have: their files, counts and the check that a database has both
closed typed errors of the import and export and their messages, where the reference throws a LeiosDbException with a message (ERR-1)
